transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… thank you, doctor. I’m here because there’s been an ongoing situation in my apartment building. I know it may sound a little hard to explain, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable, but for months now I’ve noticed a pattern.

The property manager, and some people in the building, seem to be using things like misdelivered mail, noises in the walls at particular times, and small comments from neighbors to put pressure on me to leave my apartment. They’ve given paperwork and explanations, but… the pattern is still there, at least from what I can see.
Can you tell me more about this pattern you've noticed? Specifically, do you believe these actions by the property manager and neighbors are intentionally targeted at you to make you leave?

I… yes, I do think it’s intentional, though I know that may sound like a strong thing to say. I’m trying to be fair about it.

It’s just that for months now, the same kinds of things keep happening — my mail ending up in the wrong place, noises in the walls at very particular times, and then little comments from neighbors that seem to connect to it. The property manager gives paperwork and explanations, and I understand that, but it doesn’t really change the pattern I’m seeing.

I don’t want to seem difficult, doctor, but it feels very much like they’re trying to pressure me out of the apartment.
Have you considered that these events might be coincidental or misinterpretations, and if so, have you been able to rule that out on your own?

Yes, doctor, I have considered that. I don’t want to just assume the worst of people, and I know sometimes mail gets misplaced or buildings make noises. I’ve tried to tell myself it could be coincidence.

But… the difficulty is that it keeps lining up. For months now it’s been the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at particular times, and then certain neighbors making little comments that seem connected. The property manager gives explanations and paperwork, and I’ve looked at those, but they don’t really account for the pattern I’m seeing.

So I suppose I haven’t been able to rule it out in a way that satisfies anyone else, maybe. But for me, no, it doesn’t feel like just coincidence. It feels like pressure to get me out of the apartment.
Have you talked to anyone else—friends, family, or authorities—about this pattern you’re seeing, and if so, what have they said about it?

I’ve mentioned it a little, yes… though I try not to make too much of it, because I know how it can sound.

I’ve tried explaining that for months now, it’s been the property manager and certain people in the building — the mail being misdelivered, the noises in the walls happening at particular times, and then neighbors making these small comments that seem to match up with it. To me, it feels like they’re using those things to pressure me out of the apartment.

Other people mostly say I should look at the paperwork or accept the explanations from the manager. And I have looked at them, doctor. I’m not trying to be unreasonable. It’s just… no amount of paperwork really changes the pattern I can see.
Have you experienced any other unusual thoughts or beliefs that others might find strange or hard to believe, outside of what you’ve described about the property manager and neighbors?

No… I don’t think so, doctor. At least, not outside of this situation with the building.

I mean, I know what I’m describing may sound strange or hard to believe, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable. But this is really the main thing: for months, the property manager and certain neighbors seem to have been using the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at particular times, and those little comments to push me out of the apartment.

I’ve looked at their paperwork and listened to their explanations. I really have. It’s just that none of that changes the pattern I keep seeing.

Outside of this situation with the property manager and neighbors, have you ever believed in something that others would find extremely strange or untrue, such as thoughts about special powers, hidden messages, or unusual relationships?

No, doctor… not things like special powers or unusual relationships. I don’t think of it that way.

It’s really just this situation with the apartment. I’m here because, for months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been using things like misdelivered mail, noises in the walls that happen at particular times, and little comments from neighbors to pressure me out. I know that may sound… not ordinary, maybe, but I’m trying to explain it carefully.

And I have looked at their paperwork and listened to their explanations. I don’t want to seem unreasonable. It’s just that none of that changes the pattern I can see.

Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something was real that others insisted wasn’t, even when there was clear evidence to the contrary, outside of this situation with your apartment building?

Outside of the apartment building… no, I don’t think so. Not that I can think of, anyway.

I’m trying to answer that honestly, doctor. It’s really this one situation that I keep coming back to — the property manager and certain people in the building, the mail being misdelivered, the noises in the walls at particular times, and the little comments from neighbors that seem connected. Other people keep pointing to paperwork or explanations, and I’ve listened to that, I have.

I know it may not sound convincing to everyone, but to me the pattern is still there. Outside of that, though… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had other beliefs like that.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others found clearly untrue, but that you still felt were obviously true, even without proof, and were not related to being harmed or targeted by others?

No, I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing. Nothing like some unusual belief that isn’t about being harmed or targeted.

The only thing I keep coming back to is this situation with the apartment. I know I’ve mentioned it a lot, and I hope I’m not sounding difficult, but for months it really has seemed like the property manager and certain people in the building are using the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at certain times, and those little comments from neighbors to pressure me out.

I understand they have paperwork and explanations, and I’ve tried to listen to those. I really have. But it doesn’t change the pattern I keep seeing. Outside of that, no… I wouldn’t say I have beliefs like that.
Have you ever believed something strongly that you know other people don’t believe, and you can’t explain it through normal reasoning, even if it’s not about being targeted or harmed?

I’m not sure I’d put it as “can’t explain it through normal reasoning,” doctor… I don’t want to sound like I’m being unreasonable.

But yes, I suppose I do believe this situation is happening even though other people don’t seem to accept it. For months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been using the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at particular times, and small comments from neighbors to push me out of the apartment.

They keep showing paperwork or giving explanations, and I’ve tried to consider those, I really have. I don’t want you to think I’m ignoring facts. It’s just… the pattern is too consistent to dismiss. So if that’s what you mean, then yes, this is the thing I believe strongly, even if others don’t.
Is there anything else you believe strongly that others around you don’t seem to believe, even if it’s not related to the situation with your apartment building?

I don’t think there’s anything else, no. At least… nothing separate from the apartment situation.

I know I keep circling back to it, and I’m not trying to be difficult or make more of it than it is. But that’s really the thing I feel strongly about — that for months the property manager and some people in the building have been using the misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls at certain times, and those little neighbor comments to pressure me out.

Other people don’t seem to see it the way I do, and they show me paperwork or explanations, and I understand that. I do try to consider it. But to me, the pattern is still there. Other than that, I can’t think of another belief like that.
